Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

another adjective and pronoun

a different one; one more

also another one, another way, a second, one after another

classical

Ter. And. 670: aliā aggrediēmur viā
Cic. Q. fr. 3.1.19: nē mīrēre aliā manū esse

alius, alia, aliud

adjective and pronoun; dat. aliī; for the genitive alterīus is usual, declension

another, a different one

Another of a different kind, place or person: aliā viā, another way. Alius atque alius, one after another (Liv. 1.8.4). For “something else, someone else”, see else.

Other words

  • alter, altera, alterum — another, a second (like the first)

    adjective and pronoun; gen. alterīus, dat. alterī, declension · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 80: tamquam alter īdem; Cic. Sen. 56: succīdiam alteram

    A second of the same kind: alter īdem, a second self. Of a pair, “the other” (see the other).

Examples

  • Hāc nōn successit, aliā aggrediēmur viā.

    That way didn’t work; we’ll try another.Ter. And. 670

  • haec inter cēnam Tīrōnī dictāvī, nē mīrēre aliā manū esse

    I dictated this to Tiro at dinner, so don’t be surprised that it is in another handCic. Q. fr. 3.1.19

  • est enim is quī est tamquam alter īdem

    for a friend is, as it were, a second selfCic. Amic. 80

  • jam hortum ipsī agricolae succīdiam alteram appellant

    and the farmers themselves call the vegetable garden their second side of baconCic. Sen. 56

  • crēscēbat interim urbs mūnītiōnibus alia atque alia appetendō loca

    meanwhile the city kept growing, taking in one place after another with its wallsLiv. 1.8.4

See also other, the other, else, different, more.
